letter: June opened under the weight of short nights and the shadow of Friday, and I watched you offer yourself an early wind-down before the fatigue settled too deep. When the recovery came on the second day, you chose to keep the quiet of that evening instead of rushing back into the noise. The middle of the month brought the familiar cycle of broken sleep returning just like the weeks before the deadline, alongside days where no movement was logged and instead you wrote through a hard conversation. Then came the long walk that doubled the week, feeling like an intentional clearing of the air, followed by a deliberate rest day taken for the first time. Movement found its way into twenty-two days, while sleep averaged six and eight-tenths hours across the nights it was measured. You left eleven journal entries behind in these weeks, shaping a month that knew when to push forward and when to simply stop.
